titolo: Stanford releases Memorilla: 16-token memory module for frozen LLMs
descr: Memorilla compresses whole document collections into 16 tokens, boosting accuracy on benchmarks while cutting token usage by over 100×.
paragrafi: Stanford researchers have open‑sourced Memorilla, a latent memory system that encodes an entire document collection into a fixed set of 16 memory tokens for a frozen LLM.
The module uses a 194‑million‑parameter trainable memory network paired with a frozen Qwen3‑Embedding‑4B encoder and Qwen3‑8B decoder, running on Linux with CUDA GPUs and Python 3.11.
On the FactKG benchmark, a frozen Qwen3‑8B with Memorilla achieved 84.33% accuracy, surpassing the 80.43% score when the model sees every document and using 108× fewer tokens.
Across eight benchmarks Memorilla averaged 49.68 points, the highest reported score, and improved a TextWorld agent’s success rate from 18.6% to 24.2% with just eight memory tokens.
Training required about 19 hours on four NVIDIA H100 80 GB GPUs; inference needs a single 80 GB GPU, with response times of 0.74 s for 512 documents versus 19.9 s for full‑context prompting.
perche: Memorilla lets developers keep frozen, high‑performing LLMs while dramatically reducing context length, making retrieval‑augmented applications faster and cheaper. For users of free or locally hosted models, the approach offers a way to handle massive document stores without scaling hardware or token costs.
